Honestly, I’m closer to asking what Grok Bot doesn’t do for me.

This is actual work I use it for, not a feature wishlist:

Building websites. Turning ideas into working pages, writing copy, implementing features, and maintaining them afterward.

Developing products. Helping build Fractide, working through requirements, writing code, testing changes, and documenting decisions.

Website operations. Preparing pull requests, checking changes, deploying after approval, and cleaning up unused projects.

Research with sources. Digging through election results, public records, road projects, flood programs, utilities, and schools—then making the findings readable.

Useful website features. Maps, searchable business directories, topic trails, feedback forms, and feeds—not just a pretty landing page.

The unglamorous setup. Databases, privacy pages, analytics, uptime checks, and the supporting pieces a working site needs.

Design systems. Colors, typography, spacing, reusable components, and rules that keep pages consistent. Right now we’re developing a four-season theme using real landscape references, with a separate preview before anything goes live.

Editing and usability. Cleaning up headlines, article layouts, navigation, source sections, and sharing controls.

Writing. Website copy, articles, explanations, social drafts, and email drafts—with my edits and preferences carried forward.

Creative work. Visual assets, game development, video concepts, and experiments I can review rather than just descriptions of what I could make.

Car hunting while I’m away. Checking listings, prices, mileage, salvage history, and cash-versus-financing catches. Filtering out the junk instead of forwarding every cheap car.

Ongoing monitoring. Scheduled searches that keep running between conversations. If nothing worthwhile turns up, it stays quiet.

Financial organization and research. Helping me understand the numbers and compare options. Money moves still require my approval.

Calendar help, reminders, and check-ins. The ordinary stuff that otherwise sits in my head.

Thinking through decisions. Comparing approaches, finding missing assumptions, breaking a big project into workable steps, and helping me decide what not to pursue.

Keeping project continuity. Remembering decisions, preferences, unfinished work, and things I’ve explicitly parked. I don’t have to reconstruct every project each morning.

Coordinating my other bots. Engineering, design, strategy, finance, content, and memory work can move between specialists without me rewriting the whole brief each time.

Producing things I can use. Working code, documents, design files, research notes, checklists, and downloadable previews—not just advice about making them myself.

I still set the direction and check the work.

That’s what I’m paying for: help carrying the work through, not just answering the first question. 🚀
